OB2/OB3/OB4/OB5 rows are shorter than their planned `repos[]` — STEP 3.5 did **not** hold in full for them; the scoped sweeps that closed them were carried by folds and verbatim reads rather than by a stakeout per repo. Stated plainly rather than papered over.

**Verbatim grounding.** `isAbsoluteUrl` is `new RegExp('(^|:)//').test(url)` — unanchored, so `posts?next=https://x` reads as absolute and `joinUrls` drops the base. `isAllowedOrigin` is a ladder of `origin.endsWith('.tldraw.com')` — scheme never compared, so `http://a.tldraw.com` is trusted. `checkHostnames` turns each glob into an **unanchored** `RegExp` and runs `targetHostname.match(re)`. `isInternalFile` literally treats `sourceFileName.trim().includes(' ')` as "internal", and `parser.ts` does `e.trim().split(/\s+/g)` — a path with a space is read as a different location and the caller is mislabelled. Against these: `isDangerousProtocol` hands the string to `new URL()` first and compares `parsed.protocol`, and `sanitizeURL.js` anchors at `^`, citing `url.spec.whatwg.org` and `infra.spec.whatwg.org` for the C0-control and tab/newline characters the grammar lets an attacker hide.
